questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Source: Speakers use transitions to show how ideas connect. Which paraphrase is most accurate?

answer.text: A. Transitions make speeches confusing.

feedback.text: This reverses the source meaning. The source says transitions show connections.

answer.text: B. Speakers use transitions to help listeners understand relationships between ideas.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the source meaning and changes the wording.

answer.text: C. Speakers should avoid connecting ideas.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source.

answer.text: D. Transitions are unrelated to speeches.

feedback.text: This is inaccurate because the source directly connects transitions to speaking.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.03

Source: Eye contact can make listeners feel included in a presentation. What is the key meaning?

answer.text: A. Eye contact prevents all speaking mistakes.

feedback.text: This adds a claim the source does not make.

answer.text: B. Presentations do not need listeners.

feedback.text: This contradicts the communication purpose.

answer.text: C. Eye contact should be avoided during presentations.

feedback.text: This reverses the source idea.

answer.text: D. Looking at listeners can help them feel part of the speech.

feedback.text: Correct. This restates the source meaning accurately.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Which paraphrase problem occurs when a student changes the source meaning?

answer.text: A. Inaccuracy

feedback.text: Correct. A paraphrase must keep the source meaning accurate.

answer.text: B. Strong academic vocabulary

feedback.text: Academic vocabulary can support accuracy when used correctly.

answer.text: C. Clear speech notes

feedback.text: Clear notes are helpful, not a paraphrase problem.

answer.text: D. Audience awareness

feedback.text: Audience awareness is important but does not describe changing meaning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which word is the most precise academic vocabulary for a speech lesson?

answer.text: A. stuff

feedback.text: This word is vague and informal.

answer.text: B. things

feedback.text: This word is too general for precise speech notes.

answer.text: C. transition

feedback.text: Correct. Transition is a precise communication term.

answer.text: D. whatever

feedback.text: This is informal and not academically precise.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Source: Practice helps speakers find unclear parts of a presentation. Which paraphrase is best?

answer.text: A. Rehearsing can help speakers notice which parts of a presentation need clarification.

feedback.text: Correct. This restates the meaning with new wording.

answer.text: B. Practice makes every presentation perfect.

feedback.text: This exaggerates the source and changes the meaning.

answer.text: C. Speakers should never revise unclear parts.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source.

answer.text: D. Presentations are unclear because practice is impossible.

feedback.text: This is unrelated and inaccurate.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.03

What should a speaker do before paraphrasing a complex sentence?

answer.text: A. Copy the sentence exactly.

feedback.text: Copying does not show understanding or paraphrasing.

answer.text: B. Identify the source meaning.

feedback.text: Correct. Understanding the meaning is the first step before restating it.

answer.text: C. Remove all academic words.

feedback.text: Some academic words may be necessary for accuracy.

answer.text: D. Add a personal opinion.

feedback.text: Adding an opinion can change the meaning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Which choice is closest to copying rather than paraphrasing?

answer.text: A. A new sentence that keeps the meaning.

feedback.text: This describes a valid paraphrase.

answer.text: B. A short speech note in the speaker's own words.

feedback.text: This can be useful if it stays accurate.

answer.text: C. The original sentence with only one or two words changed.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps too much of the source wording and structure.

answer.text: D. A restatement that changes the sentence pattern.

feedback.text: Changing structure is part of paraphrasing.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Source: Note cards can keep a speaker from losing the order of ideas. Which paraphrase is accurate?

answer.text: A. Note cards cause speakers to forget ideas.

feedback.text: This reverses the source meaning.

answer.text: B. Speakers should write every word on note cards.

feedback.text: This adds a claim that is not in the source.

answer.text: C. Ideas do not need order during a speech.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source.

answer.text: D. Note cards can help speakers remember the sequence of their ideas.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the meaning and uses new wording.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Why might a paraphrase keep the word audience?

answer.text: A. It is a precise communication term needed for meaning.

feedback.text: Correct. Some academic terms should stay because they name important concepts.

answer.text: B. It makes the paraphrase longer for no reason.

feedback.text: Length is not the purpose of keeping academic vocabulary.

answer.text: C. It hides the source meaning.

feedback.text: Precise vocabulary should clarify meaning, not hide it.

answer.text: D. It makes the paraphrase informal.

feedback.text: Audience is an appropriate academic communication word.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Source: A summary includes only the most important ideas from a longer text. Which statement is true?

answer.text: A. A summary must include every sentence from the source.

feedback.text: A summary is shorter and includes only the most important ideas.

answer.text: B. A summary should change the source meaning.

feedback.text: A summary must stay accurate.

answer.text: C. A summary is always longer than the source.

feedback.text: A summary is usually shorter than the source.

answer.text: D. A summary is shorter and focuses on the main ideas.

feedback.text: Correct. This describes the difference between summary and full source text.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.03

Source: Speakers should check whether their evidence clearly supports the point being made. What is the meaning?

answer.text: A. Evidence should be unrelated to the point.

feedback.text: This reverses the source meaning.

answer.text: B. Speakers need to make sure evidence connects to the point.

feedback.text: Correct. This accurately restates the meaning.

answer.text: C. Points do not need evidence.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source.

answer.text: D. Evidence is only for written work.

feedback.text: The source applies evidence to speaking.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Which paraphrase changes the meaning of this source: Clear notes help speakers deliver information smoothly.

answer.text: A. Organized notes can help a speaker present information more smoothly.

feedback.text: This keeps the original meaning.

answer.text: B. Speakers may deliver information more smoothly when their notes are clear.

feedback.text: This accurately restates the source.

answer.text: C. Clear notes make speaking unnecessary.

feedback.text: Correct. This changes the meaning because notes support speaking; they do not replace it.

answer.text: D. Notes that are easy to follow can support smooth delivery.

feedback.text: This is an accurate paraphrase.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

What is the best speech note from this source: A speaker should pause briefly after a major point so the audience can process the idea.

answer.text: A. Pause after major point; audience needs time to process.

feedback.text: Correct. This is concise and keeps the source meaning for speaking.

answer.text: B. A speaker should pause briefly after a major point so the audience can process the idea.

feedback.text: This copies the source instead of making a note.

answer.text: C. Never pause during a speech.

feedback.text: This changes the source meaning.

answer.text: D. Audience processing does not matter.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which phrase uses academic vocabulary most appropriately?

answer.text: A. Talk thing

feedback.text: This is vague and informal.

answer.text: B. Speech stuff

feedback.text: This does not use precise academic language.

answer.text: C. Some speaking things

feedback.text: This is vague and not useful for notes.

answer.text: D. Presentation structure

feedback.text: Correct. This phrase is precise and appropriate for speech notes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Source: An effective conclusion reminds the audience of the speech's central idea. Which paraphrase is best?

answer.text: A. A strong closing brings listeners back to the main focus of the speech.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the meaning with new wording.

answer.text: B. Conclusions should introduce an unrelated topic.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source.

answer.text: C. The audience should forget the central idea.

feedback.text: This reverses the source meaning.

answer.text: D. A conclusion is only a list of random facts.

feedback.text: This is inaccurate and unfocused.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.03

When reading a source for speech notes, what should the speaker identify?

answer.text: A. Only the longest word.

feedback.text: The longest word may not be the most important idea.

answer.text: B. The important idea and supporting meaning.

feedback.text: Correct. These are needed for accurate paraphrasing.

answer.text: C. A new opinion to add.

feedback.text: Adding opinion can change the source meaning.

answer.text: D. A way to avoid the source meaning.

feedback.text: Avoiding meaning prevents accurate paraphrasing.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Which choice best describes a paraphrase?

answer.text: A. A copied sentence with quotation marks removed.

feedback.text: This is copying, not paraphrasing.

answer.text: B. A personal opinion about the source.

feedback.text: A paraphrase restates the source, not the speaker's opinion.

answer.text: C. A restatement of source information in new wording that keeps the meaning.

feedback.text: Correct. This defines accurate paraphrasing.

answer.text: D. A sentence that removes the main idea.

feedback.text: Removing the main idea makes the paraphrase inaccurate.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Source: Visual aids can support a speech when they clarify information for the audience. Which paraphrase is accurate?

answer.text: A. Visual aids are helpful when they make speech information clearer for listeners.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the meaning and changes the wording.

answer.text: B. Visual aids always replace speaking.

feedback.text: This adds an incorrect claim.

answer.text: C. Audiences should ignore visual aids.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source.

answer.text: D. Visual aids are never connected to information.

feedback.text: This reverses the source meaning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which word pair is most useful for academic speech notes?

answer.text: A. stuff and things

feedback.text: These are vague words because they do not name a clear communication idea.

answer.text: B. whatever and maybe

feedback.text: These are informal and imprecise.

answer.text: C. focus and evidence

feedback.text: Correct. These are precise academic communication words.

answer.text: D. cool and random

feedback.text: These are informal and not specific enough.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

What should a speaker do after writing a paraphrase?

answer.text: A. Never compare it to the source.

feedback.text: Comparison helps check accuracy.

answer.text: B. Assume it is correct because it is shorter.

feedback.text: Shorter does not always mean accurate.

answer.text: C. Add unrelated facts to make it longer.

feedback.text: Unrelated facts change the meaning and weaken notes.

answer.text: D. Compare it with the source to check meaning.

feedback.text: Correct. Checking helps ensure the paraphrase is accurate.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.03

Source: Complex texts may require rereading before a speaker can explain them clearly. What does this mean?

answer.text: A. A speaker may need to read a difficult source more than once to understand it.

feedback.text: Correct. This captures the source meaning.

answer.text: B. Speakers should avoid all complex texts.

feedback.text: The source says rereading may help, not that complex texts should be avoided.

answer.text: C. Rereading makes explanation impossible.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source.

answer.text: D. Clear explanation does not require understanding.

feedback.text: Understanding is necessary for clear explanation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Which paraphrase is too close to the source: Speakers can use brief notes to avoid reading every word.

answer.text: A. Short notes can help speakers avoid reading word for word.

feedback.text: This is accurate but somewhat close; it changes enough to be a paraphrase.

answer.text: B. Speakers can use brief notes to avoid reading every word.

feedback.text: Correct. This copies the source exactly.

answer.text: C. Brief speaker notes can support natural delivery.

feedback.text: This restates the idea more generally.

answer.text: D. Notes with only key ideas can keep a speaker from reading the whole speech.

feedback.text: This changes wording and structure while keeping meaning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Why are paraphrased notes useful in speeches?

answer.text: A. They allow speakers to ignore source meaning.

feedback.text: Ignoring meaning leads to inaccurate communication.

answer.text: B. They make speakers read directly from the source.

feedback.text: Paraphrased notes should support natural explanation.

answer.text: C. They help speakers explain source ideas in their own words.

feedback.text: Correct. This is the purpose of paraphrased speech notes.

answer.text: D. They remove all academic vocabulary.

feedback.text: Useful notes may keep needed academic words.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which revision makes a speech note more precise?

answer.text: A. Change "audience response" to "stuff."

feedback.text: This makes the note less precise.

answer.text: B. Change "evidence" to "thing."

feedback.text: This removes useful academic vocabulary.

answer.text: C. Change "transition" to "whatever comes next."

feedback.text: This is informal and less precise.

answer.text: D. Change "talk part" to "main point."

feedback.text: Correct. Main point is precise academic speech vocabulary.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_Quiz_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Which statement best summarizes this lesson?

answer.text: A. A speaker should understand source meaning and restate it accurately in their own words for speech notes.

feedback.text: Correct. This captures the lesson focus on accurate paraphrasing.

answer.text: B. A speaker should copy every source sentence into the speech.

feedback.text: Copying does not show paraphrase or natural speech preparation.

answer.text: C. A speaker should change the meaning to make the speech more exciting.

feedback.text: Changing meaning makes the paraphrase inaccurate.

answer.text: D. A speaker should avoid all academic vocabulary.

feedback.text: Precise academic vocabulary can be useful when it is accurate.
